outcome: The best known bound in the plane (d=2, dimension > 5/4, Guth–Iosevich–Ou–Wang 2020) has not been improved since 26 January 2024, and the best known bound in higher dimensions (d/2 + 1/4 − 1/(8d+4) for d≥3) was already fixed in a preprint submitted 8 September 2023 (arXiv:2309.04103 v1) — before the frozen revision's date — and was not mathematically changed by the October 2024 v2 revision, which the authors' own revision note describes as having 'slightly changed the introduction' only. The conjecture itself remains open in every dimension; only case-restricted or related variant results appeared inside the window.
summary: Falconer's conjecture (Hausdorff dimension > d/2 in ℝ^d implies a distance set of nonzero Lebesgue measure) remains open in every dimension as of September 2026. The only substantive advance anywhere near the window is Du–Ou–Ren–Zhang's improvement of the higher-dimensional (d≥3) threshold to d/2 + 1/4 − 1/(8d+4), but this bound was fixed in arXiv:2309.04103 v1, submitted 8 September 2023 — more than four months before the frozen revision's 26 January 2024 timestamp. A v2 was posted 22 October 2024 (inside the window), but I fetched the arXiv abstract page directly and its own revision note says only '33 pages; slightly changed the introduction', with the file growing from 38KB to 40KB; the abstract and the stated bound are identical between versions, so no mathematics changed. The April 2024 Quanta Magazine article, read directly, is press coverage of the pre-existing 2023 result, not a report of new mathematics — it names no event past September 2023. The current Wikipedia 'Falconer's conjecture' article (fetched directly, last edited 18 September 2026) still cites this same 2023 Du–Ou–Ren–Zhang bound as the best known result in higher dimensions and 5/4 (Guth–Iosevich–Ou–Wang 2020, itself pre-2024) as the best known bound in the plane — confirming independently that nothing has superseded either bound in the window. A background research agent additionally found three papers submitted inside the window (arXiv:2503.15709 on nonempty interior, a strictly stronger and different property than positive measure; arXiv:2510.15118 proving the conjecture only for restricted hyperplane/product-set cases; arXiv:2607.05926 on the discrete finite-field Erdős–Falconer analogue, a different problem over vector spaces rather than ℝ^d) and a direct search of Terence Tao's blog and of Wikipedia's 'List of mathematical discoveries by artificial intelligence' page, both of which surfaced nothing relevant. None of the case/variant papers change the stated d/2 threshold or resolve any fixed dimension, so per §3.1 they do not move the status off open, and per §6.1 the correct code is open_stale rather than open, since the one bound-moving event on record predates the frozen revision even though it was still being publicized and lightly revised within the window. No AI system was mentioned in any source I or the research agent examined in connection with this problem.
competing_reading: One could argue for `progress` dated to 9 April 2024 (the Quanta article) or to 22 October 2024 (the v2 arXiv revision) on the theory that the bound only became widely known, or was formally re-submitted, inside the window. But §6.3 requires dating to the first public written argument, which is the 8 September 2023 v1 submission — press coverage and a cosmetic revision are not new events under that rule, so I classify as `open_stale` rather than `progress`. If a reader considers the widely-publicized Quanta coverage itself the 'event' that made the bound part of the record within the window, `progress` with event date 2024-04-09 and resolution_direction null would be the alternative record.
what_would_settle_it: A revision history diff of arXiv:2309.04103 v1 vs v2 showing whether the stated theorem, its dimension threshold, or its proof changed in any way beyond the introduction wording; this would confirm or overturn the open_stale classification. Also, any post-2024 paper improving the plane bound past 5/4 or the higher-dimensional bound past d/2 + 1/4 − 1/(8d+4) would move the status to `progress`.
